simple.meaning: חָטַף (châṭaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to clutch ; hence, to seize as a prisoner.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Judges, Psalms, beginning at Judges 21:21. The surrounding contexts include family line, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָטַף (H2414) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חָטַף (châṭaph) / H2414 is traced through Judges 21:21, Psalms 10:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to clutch ; hence, to seize as a prisoner
